test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is a correct use of electromagnets?

I. In separating magnetic material from junk

II. In sharpening pencils
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electromagnets** are temporary magnets that consist of a coil of wire wrapped around a **soft iron core**, which becomes magnetized only when an **electric current** flows through the coil.
 
• **Statement I** is correct because **electromagnets** are extensively used in **cranes** at junk yards and recycling centers to separate **magnetic substances** like **iron** and **steel** from non-magnetic scrap material.
 
• **Statement II** is incorrect because **sharpening pencils** is a **mechanical process** involving **cutting blades** or **abrasive surfaces** to shave away wood; it does not utilize **magnetic fields** or **electromagnetic induction**.
 
• The strength of an **electromagnet** can be easily controlled by changing the amount of **electric current** or the number of turns in the **solenoid**, making it ideal for industrial lifting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnets** are used in various daily appliances such as **electric bells**, **loudspeakers**, **headphones**, and **electric motors**.
 
• In the field of **medicine**, they are a critical component of **Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)** scanners, which help in visualizing the internal structures of the body.
 
• **Maglev (Magnetic Levitation)** trains use powerful **electromagnets** to lift and propel the train above the tracks, eliminating **friction** and allowing for extremely high speeds.
 
• Unlike **permanent magnets**, the magnetism of an **electromagnet** can be turned **ON** or **OFF** instantly by controlling the power supply.
